claims.text: Uncertainty in large language models can be estimated at the level of semantic meaning rather than specific sequence of words.
Semantic entropy uncertainty estimators detect confabulations in large language models.

evidence.description: Our method addresses the fact that one idea can be expressed in many ways by computing uncertainty at the level of meaning rather than specific sequences of words.
proposing entropy-based uncertainty estimators for LLMs to detect a subset of hallucinations—confabulations—which are arbitrary and incorrect generations.

methodologies.name: Semantic Entropy Uncertainty Estimation
methodologies.description: A statistical method calculating uncertainty at the semantic meaning level rather than over raw token sequences to identify arbitrary, incorrect generations in LLMs.
conditions: without a priori knowledge of the task

limitations.text: Encouraging truthfulness through supervision or reinforcement has been only partially successful.
The proposed method detects only a specific subset of hallucinations (confabulations).
